instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: The document is a Draft 2020-12 object schema identified as pm.goal_runtime_events.schema.v1 and titled Puppet Master Goal Runtime Event.
atoms.title: Explicit root schema identity

atoms.statement: The event envelope is closed at the root because additionalProperties is false.
atoms.title: Closed top-level event envelope

atoms.statement: The schema requires event identity and time, project and goal identity, revision, actor and role, requested and effective provider/model/account refs, correlation, evidence and artifact arrays, and payload.
atoms.title: Common required event envelope

atoms.statement: event_name is restricted to twenty-one goal and goal_run event names spanning creation through terminal and exceptional outcomes.
atoms.title: Finite goal runtime event vocabulary

atoms.statement: payload is only required to be a nonempty object; there are no event_name-discriminated schemas defining required fields, types, invariants, or forbidden combinations for any event.
atoms.title: Event payload semantics are untyped

atoms.statement: One invariant required-field set applies to every event_name, with no conditional distinction between lifecycle facts, execution facts, approval facts, blocking facts, and parent-child facts.
atoms.title: Required fields do not vary by event semantics

atoms.statement: thread_id, parent_goal_id, causation_event_ref, idempotency_key, approval_ref, and block_ref are optional unconstrained strings that permit empty values and have no event-specific dependency rules.
atoms.title: Control and linkage references are underconstrained

atoms.statement: The envelope has no required unique event identifier, and idempotency_key is optional and permits an empty string.
atoms.title: Retry and duplicate-event semantics are not enforceable

atoms.statement: evidence_refs and artifact_refs constrain only each present element; they have no minItems, maxItems, or uniqueItems constraints.
atoms.title: Evidence and artifact arrays lack cardinality limits

atoms.statement: payload has no properties, additionalProperties, nesting, value-type, or size constraints beyond being a nonempty object.
atoms.title: Payload admits arbitrary unbounded data

atoms.statement: Actor, role, provider, model, and account references are nonempty strings without format, namespace, project-binding, authorization, or requested-to-effective transition rules.
atoms.title: Authority-bearing references are structurally opaque

atoms.statement: goal_revision is required, but expected_goal_revision and causation_event_ref are optional and no constraints relate revisions, causation, event_name, or prior state.
atoms.title: Event ordering and transition legality are external

atoms.statement: The schema supplies concrete field-level oracles for schema version, timestamp shape, nonempty core references, and positive revisions.
atoms.title: Core primitive validation oracles are explicit

atoms.statement: The closed root and constant v1 field create a strict version boundary without any in-schema compatibility or migration mechanism.
atoms.title: Version evolution policy is unspecified

atoms.statement: The schema names runtime facts but defines no producer ownership, subscriber set, projection rules, GUI mapping, localization or accessibility behavior, or support-facing observability contract.
atoms.title: Consumer and GUI interpretations are outside the schema

atoms.statement: The vocabulary includes degraded, blocked, cancelled, stopped, receipt, and certified facts, but the envelope has no delivery acknowledgement, retry state, recovery action, compensating-event, or rollback linkage contract.
atoms.title: Failure events lack delivery and recovery semantics

atoms.statement: The owner text requires lineage preservation on every child lifecycle path and clamps tool, write, FileSafe, mode, provider/model/account, and crew authority before dispatch, with audit after completion.
atoms.title: Child lineage and effective-authority ceiling are explicit

atoms.statement: The exact contract retires tier/FIFO execution ownership in favor of DAG readiness, a scored ready-set, package/seam lane capacity, and package-based worktree allocation with quarantine and safe-point recovery.
atoms.title: Graph-native scheduling and package/seam lane ownership are named

atoms.statement: The source repeatedly makes a scored ready-set canonical and calls fallbacks deterministic, but it does not define score inputs, ordering, tie-breaking, aging, starvation prevention, or how wake reasons change priority under sustained capacity pressure.
atoms.title: Scored ready-set has no score, tie-break, aging, or starvation contract

atoms.statement: The contract requires rejection of unsafe self-dispatch loops but never identifies the identity comparison, graph-cycle rule, recursion ceiling, rejection outcome, or test fixture that proves direct and indirect loops are stopped.
atoms.title: Unsafe self-dispatch rejection lacks a detection and test oracle

atoms.statement: Permission gates, visible cards, and evidence receipts are required, but the source does not define URL/header/cookie/form/console redaction, sensitive-page denial, evidence retention/deletion, iframe-origin handling, or what child and parent views may disclose.
atoms.title: Delegated web/browser evidence lacks a privacy and data-lifecycle contract

atoms.statement: The orchestrator may silently continue with fewer acceptance criteria when the optional strategy file is invalid; there is no required run-receipt bit, GUI state, or promotion rule distinguishing full criteria from degraded criteria.
atoms.title: Invalid test-strategy input is WARN-only without criteria-integrity disclosure

atoms.statement: Children do not get a direct user channel; clarification is routed through the parent question flow, preserving parent ownership of user interaction.
atoms.title: User-question escalation is explicitly parent-mediated

atoms.statement: OSI-431 explicitly binds host capability context to parent goal, run mode, execution-unit, worktree/jail, permission, FileSafe, and host ceilings and preserves blocked host families for parent synthesis.
atoms.title: OSI-431 defines a strong containerized-host child clamp

atoms.statement: The PlanUnit's executable runtime invariant is not paired with a present fixture: plan-index validation can validate metadata, while the only host-authority fixture is explicitly future work.
atoms.title: OSI-431 runtime enforcement is backed only by a future fixture

atoms.statement: After declaring tier vocabulary compatibility-only and graph/package/seam/lane identity canonical, the integration code still selects, routes, identifies, and builds context around TierNode, TierType, select_for_tier, and tier overrides without a normalization boundary.
atoms.title: Normative-looking implementation code revives the retired tier ontology

atoms.statement: The coordination key is only subagent name plus tier-node id, while the ActiveAgent record omits run, thread, parent-child, attempt, package, seam, and lane identity required by the owner contract.
atoms.title: ActiveAgent identity can collide across runs and attempts

atoms.statement: Both parallel result propagation and sequential child execution can return before the later unregister loop; no finally/drop guard, cancellation fan-out, idempotent teardown, or reconciliation path is specified.
atoms.title: Error propagation bypasses coordination cleanup

atoms.statement: The error policy says registration and updates warn and continue, but the sample uses `await?` for registration, activity updates, file updates, and unregister; no authoritative precedence or event outcome resolves the mismatch.
atoms.title: Best-effort coordination prose contradicts fail-fast code

atoms.statement: The accepted PlanUnit names host_capability_ref, host_profile_id, host_assignment_id, host receipts, and blocked payloads, but the invocation and ExecutionUnitContext sample carry none of them and identify no caller that supplies or reconciles them.
atoms.title: OSI-431 host capability and receipt fields are not wired into the shown child invocation

atoms.statement: File paths extracted from child findings or later free-text parsing are written into coordination state without defining canonicalization, workspace containment, symlink handling, existence checks, lease ownership, or FileSafe validation.
atoms.title: Model-reported file operations are trusted without FileSafe normalization

atoms.statement: The code obtains one platform and model for the tier and passes them to all children; it does not show the required concrete provider entry, requested/effective account, Persona, effort, or selection receipt per child.
atoms.title: Per-child effective provider/account selection is collapsed to one tier platform/model

atoms.statement: The prologue forbids later prose from introducing competing parallel caps, yet SubagentPolicy defines normal and hard parallel/wave/time/tool limits as canonical runtime defaults without an exact mapping to the executionLimits owner.
atoms.title: SubagentPolicy reintroduces parallel limits that the prologue assigns to executionLimits SSOT

atoms.statement: The allocation text defines eligibility, quarantine, and cleanup predicates but not atomic lease acquisition, compare-and-swap ownership, fencing tokens, renewal/expiry, crash takeover, or double-release behavior.
atoms.title: Worktree lease semantics omit atomicity and fencing

atoms.statement: The GUI/receipt consumer snapshot includes repo_root and worktree_path plus branch and commit metadata, but no redaction, remote-support export, tenancy boundary, retention, or local-machine disclosure rules are defined.
atoms.title: SCM projection exposes local paths without disclosure policy

atoms.statement: The prose requires a clear skip message, but the example returns immediately when the gate is absent and therefore provides neither a test failure nor observable skipped-evidence receipt.
atoms.title: Environment-gated smoke examples silently pass without running

atoms.statement: The invocation example accepts any non-empty output, while plan-mode verification makes honoring the mode optional and suggests checking only that flags appeared; neither oracle proves role application, read-only behavior, or absence of writes.
atoms.title: Invocation and plan-mode assertions do not prove the promised behavior

atoms.statement: The test sections repeatedly allow ad hoc evidence log files even though the rewrite section says replayable run history must use the unified seglog and forbids one-off log files; ownership, retention, and redaction are unresolved.
atoms.title: Optional raw CLI evidence logs compete with the canonical event stream

atoms.statement: The source explicitly permits delegated analysis in ask/plan while prohibiting silent widening into execution authority and requires required/optional classification.
atoms.title: Planning children remain read-only under the parent mode ceiling

atoms.statement: The retry policy names provider_transient, rate_limit, and tool_timeout, but does not define offline detection, partial-stream durability, idempotency keys, reconnect/resume versus reroute, duplicated tool effects, or parent/child state reconciliation after connection loss.
atoms.title: Offline and mid-stream network-loss recovery is unspecified

atoms.statement: The example says never hardcode agent/cursor-agent but supplies `agent` as the fallback and hardcodes a platform-specific function, leaving migration behavior dependent on stale binary assumptions.
atoms.title: Test helper hardcodes a provider binary despite its own DRY prohibition

atoms.statement: The source specifies persisted global state, tier-value synchronization, disabling of subordinate controls, Wizard defaults, and a one-click action, providing concrete GUI/backend behavior for the legacy tier projection.
atoms.title: Global and per-tier plan-mode GUI behavior is specified end to end

atoms.statement: The GUI/backend section declares all tier plan-mode and subagent items in scope now and persists four-tier controls, while the document's owner contract says tier language is compatibility-only and active runtime policy is graph/package/seam/lane based; no projection-to-canonical mapping or effective-state disclosure is specified.
atoms.title: In-scope GUI makes retired tier controls look like live execution authority

atoms.statement: Provider-native agent files can be imported and their instructions normalized by an AI pass, but the source does not require quarantine, prompt-injection detection, provenance display before activation, size/encoding limits, capability stripping, review/approval, or rollback to the exact imported body.
atoms.title: Persona import and AI trimming lack untrusted-content controls

atoms.statement: Users may delete any imported or user-created Persona, but the plan does not define confirmation, undo/tombstone retention, behavior for bound subagent entries and active/frozen runs, or how audit history resolves a deleted Persona.
atoms.title: Persona deletion has no dependency, confirmation, or rollback contract

atoms.statement: One resolution says retry exhaustion creates a partial output and completes with warnings; the next says generic extraction plus retry exhaustion is a Provider error surfaced to the user with Retry/Skip/View raw output. No precedence, canonical state, or transition defines which outcome applies.
atoms.title: Parser exhaustion has two incompatible terminal outcomes

atoms.statement: The parser contract logs an initial excerpt and preserves all raw output, then offers a user-facing raw-output view, without secret detection, tool-argument redaction, retention duration, access control, size limits, or support-export policy.
atoms.title: Raw provider output retention and display lack redaction boundaries

atoms.statement: The detailed toggles, buttons, list editors, errors, tooltips, Persona previews, and retry actions do not specify accessible names, keyboard/focus behavior, screen-reader status announcements, contrast/error semantics, localization keys, pluralization, text expansion, or right-to-left layout.
atoms.title: GUI specifications omit accessibility and localization contracts

atoms.statement: The delegated contract says provider-native subagent syntax is not normative, and DRY rules prohibit platform match statements, but the mitigation prescribes a Cursor slash-prefix adapter and says a new platform can be added by a match arm or config entry.
atoms.title: Provider-native subagent syntax is both forbidden and prescribed

atoms.statement: The source requires invalidation on config/workspace changes but merely suggests either a TTL or run-duration cache; it does not define file-change invalidation, canonical-path failures, symlink retargeting, multi-project isolation, or which stale result is safe.
atoms.title: Project-context cache freshness remains an open implementation choice

atoms.statement: The source resolves two otherwise ambiguous selection edges: required entries win over disabled entries, and missing or empty overrides preserve auto-selection.
atoms.title: Required/disabled conflict and empty override semantics are deterministic

atoms.statement: The mitigation does not choose between explicit save, autosave, and dirty-state prompting and does not define atomic write, crash recovery, partial serialization failure, cross-tab concurrency, or rollback behavior.
atoms.title: Config durability behavior remains 'save and/or prompt'

atoms.statement: The resolved soft-cap rule force-completes after max+1 and never rejects valid answers, but the later wiring instruction still leaves over-max behavior as 'either reject or accept depending on product rule.'
atoms.title: Interview max-question transition is both resolved and unresolved

atoms.statement: The numeric contract defines defaults, optional unlimited max, and max+1 arithmetic but not min<=max, zero handling, per-phase override precedence, integer bounds/overflow, migration from the old field, or validation errors shown to users.
atoms.title: Interview min/max domain validation is absent

atoms.statement: The max-question rule force-completes a phase without an exception for confirmation gates, while require_architecture_confirmation says the flow must wait for explicit confirmation before allowing phase completion; precedence and recovery are not defined.
atoms.title: Force-completion can bypass required architecture confirmation

atoms.statement: The plan requires adding a string field and selecting vision-capable requests, but explicitly permits wiring the field without runtime behavior if no image flow exists, contradicting the later no-dead-fields wiring rule and leaving requested/effective provider disclosure absent.
atoms.title: vision_provider is allowed to remain a dead execution field

atoms.statement: The validator is required to prove that configuration is present and actually used, yet its proposed inputs are only tier type, config snapshot, and context; no runtime-use instrumentation, provenance token, consumed-field trace, or mutation-based test oracle is defined.
atoms.title: Config-snapshot validator cannot prove a field is actually used

atoms.statement: The text recommends fail-fast for required execution fields but leaves optional-field defaults to product choice, and the sample exposes a general WarnAndContinue policy even for VerificationStatus::Fail; no non-overridable failure class protects required authority/config invariants.
atoms.title: Required-field failure can still be warn-and-continue

atoms.statement: The lifecycle alignment says verification is persisted as seglog/redb and not authoritative ad hoc JSON, while the responsibility list mandates `.puppet-master/logs/verification.log`; the prologue separately forbids one-off run-history logs, with no projection/diagnostic distinction or retention owner.
atoms.title: Verification persistence requires both canonical events and a forbidden ad hoc log

atoms.statement: The UI wiring check is conditional on both directory existence and the node scope involving UI work, but the source does not define the classifier, owner, false-negative behavior, generated/dynamic UI handling, or a required failure when scope metadata is missing.
atoms.title: UI-scope detection is an unowned bypass point

atoms.statement: The plan requires full checks and a reviewer at every end boundary, retry, and quality failure, but does not reconcile this fan-out with parent budgets, lane capacity, deduplication, cancellation, priority, or behavior when the reviewer itself fails or times out.
atoms.title: Full boundary verification has no bounded cost or overload behavior
